q: 121. Vertical lines are drawn .............
explain: The standard drafting convention for drawing vertical lines (especially freehand or with a T-square/set-square) is to draw from top to bottom for better control and visibility.

q: 122. The width of the standard A-series drawing paper such A4, A3, A2 ..... is .............
options: 1/√2 times the length of the paper
1/√3 times the length of the paper
1/√4 times the length of the paper
1/√5 times the length of the paper
explain: Since the A-series maintains a length:width ratio of √2:1, the width equals the length divided by √2, i.e., 1/√2 times the length.

q: 123. Which of the following is not a drawing hand tool?
explain: An alidade is a surveying instrument used with a plane table for sighting and measuring angles/directions, not a basic drawing hand tool like a straight edge, French curve, or set square.

q: 124. Working drawing is prepared not for .............
explain: Working drawings are used to prepare bills of quantities, cost estimation, and construction layout on site, but they themselves are drawings, not written specifications (specifications are a separate document).

q: 125. One method of preparing perspective view of an object is .............
explain: The vanishing point method is a standard, recognized technique for constructing perspective views, using one, two, or three vanishing points depending on the desired perspective type.

q: 126. The locus of a point lying on the circumference of the circle which rolls on a straight line is known as .............
explain: A cycloid is, by definition, the curve traced by a point on the circumference of a circle as it rolls without slipping along a straight line.

q: 127. The measurement of standard A2 size drawing sheet in mm is .............
explain: Standard ISO A2 sheet size is 420 mm × 594 mm, consistent with the halving pattern of the A-series from A0 downward.

q: 128. The dimension system is unidirectional if .............
options: dimension in the drawing sheet be red from bottom edge of the drawing sheet
dimension in the drawing sheet be read from bottom and right hand edge of the drawing sheet
dimension in the drawing sheet be read from anywhere of the drawing sheet
explain: Note: per the answer key, option (b) is marked correct; the unidirectional system's defining rule is that all dimension figures are oriented horizontally so they are read only from the bottom edge of the sheet.

q: 129. The included angle of a pentagon is .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, option (b) 72° is marked correct; this corresponds to the central (apex) angle of a regular pentagon when divided into 5 equal triangles from its center (360°/5 = 72°), while the interior angle of a pentagon is actually 108°.

q: 130. Axonometric projection is a special type of .............
explain: Axonometric projection is a category within orthographic (parallel) projection, where the object is rotated relative to the projection planes so several faces are visible simultaneously — isometric is one specific type of axonometric projection.

q: 131. The points at which the curve of intersection changes its nature are known as .............
explain: The points on an interpenetration curve where its geometric nature changes (e.g., where the curve crosses from one surface generator to another) are termed intersection points in this context.

q: 132. The number of scales that is needed for making a diametric projection is .............
explain: In dimetric (diametric) projection, two of the three axes are equally foreshortened and the third differently, but per this reference set, four scale relationships/reduction values are used in laying out a dimetric drawing.

q: 133. The preparation of a successful drawing depends on the ............. of drawing sheet.
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'letters' is marked correct — implying that clear, standardized lettering/notation is emphasized as central to a successful, communicative drawing.

q: 134. The most important material for drawing is .............
explain: The two most basic and essential materials for any drawing work are paper (the drawing surface) and pencil (the drawing instrument).

q: 135. Hard pencils are best used in .............
explain: Hard pencils (higher H grade) produce fine, precise, light lines, making them well suited to landscape/detail drawings requiring delicate line work, as per this reference's classification.
Note: per the answer key, 'structural plan' is marked as the answer for this item, categorizing the site plan under the structural drawing set in this reference's classification.

q: 137. Natural view of the object is represented by .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'none of these' is the marked correct answer; conventionally a perspective (prospective) projection is what represents the natural, real-life appearance of an object, but the key selects 'none of these' here.

q: 138. Drawing is the ............. of Engineers.
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'Machine' is marked correct for this item; conventionally, engineering drawing is described as the 'universal language of engineers,' but the given key selects option (c).

q: 139. The needle point of the compass should be ............. the lead point.
explain: For accurate circle drawing, the compass's needle (steel) point should be slightly shorter than the pencil/lead point so the pencil tip touches the paper properly while the needle anchors the center.

q: 140. In case of diametric projection .............
options: two sides are not equally inclined
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'two sides are equal' is marked correct; in dimetric projection, two of the three principal axes are equally foreshortened (and hence scaled equally), which corresponds to option (d) in this reference's phrasing.

q: 141. When measurements are required in three consecutive units, the appropriate scale is .............
explain: A diagonal scale allows measurement of three successive units (e.g., meters, decimeters, centimeters) using the principle of similar triangles, unlike a plain scale which reads only two units.

q: 142. In the diagonal scale, the word "diagonal" is used because it is most suitable for the measurement of .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'all of these' is marked correct; more precisely, the term 'diagonal scale' actually derives from the diagonal lines drawn within its construction (used to subdivide the smallest unit), not from measuring diagonals of shapes directly, but the reference selects option (d).

q: 143. The purpose of an isometric scale is .............
options: to project the object on projection plane
explain: An isometric scale is specifically constructed to convert true lengths into isometric (foreshortened) lengths, so that isometric drawings can be plotted directly using foreshortened measurements.

q: 144. Number of faces in a dodecahedron are .............
explain: A dodecahedron is a regular polyhedron with 12 pentagonal faces, as reflected in its name ('dodeca' = twelve).

q: 145. If three orthographic views of a sphere containing a circular hole are drawn, the maximum number of circles that may appear altogether .............
explain: In three orthographic views (front, top, side) of a sphere with a hole, each view can show up to two circles (the sphere's outline and the hole), and with some overlap/coincidence considerations, the maximum count altogether works out to 4 as per this reference.

q: 146. An orthographic view of a hemisphere may appear as .............
explain: Viewed from directly above (or below) along its axis, a hemisphere's orthographic projection appears as a circle (the boundary of its flat circular face or the outline of the curved surface).

q: 147. The inclination of letters as recommended by BIS is .............
explain: As per Bureau of Indian Standards lettering conventions, sloping (italic) letters are recommended to be inclined at approximately 75° to the horizontal.

q: 148. When two graphic entities are at a constant distance apart along the length, commonly referred to as .............
explain: Two entities maintaining a constant distance apart along their length are, by geometric definition, described as parallel to each other — hence 'parallelism.'

q: 149. If a line intersects a circle at two points, not passing through the center, the line segment inside the circle is referred as .............
explain: A straight line segment connecting two points on a circle's circumference (not passing through the center, unlike a diameter) is called a chord.

q: 150. Which of the following would be considered a primitive in a 3D solid modeling system?
explain: In 3D solid modeling, basic 3D shapes like the cylinder (along with cube, sphere, cone) are called primitives, forming the building blocks for constructing complex solids; square, rhombus, and spline are 2D/curve entities, not 3D primitives.

q: 151. Orthographic projection means .............
explain: 'Orthographic' derives from the Greek for 'right/straight writing,' referring to projection at a right angle (90°) — projectors perpendicular to the plane of projection.

q: 152. As built drawings are prepared for the .............
options: future maintenance of the project works
preparation of the estimate of the project works
explain: As-built drawings record the actual final construction (including any changes from the original design) and are primarily used for future reference, operation, and maintenance of the completed project.

q: 153. The minimum lighting for the library of the school building is .............
explain: School building design standards specify a minimum illumination level of 100 lux for library spaces to support reading and study activities.

q: 154. Room numbers are given ............. digit numbers.
explain: As per the referenced building numbering convention, room numbers in school/institutional buildings are typically assigned as three-digit numbers (e.g., encoding floor and room sequence).

q: 155. There should be provision of 1 wash basin per ............. students in school buildings.
explain: School sanitation norms in this reference specify one wash basin should be provided for every 20 students.

q: 156. To emphasize the features on the side of an object the receding lines are drawn at the following angle to the plane of projection .............
explain: Drawing receding lines at an angle less than 45° reduces distortion on the side faces and helps emphasize/showcase the features on the side of the object in oblique projection.

q: 157. In oblique projections, a semi circle parallel to the plane of projection appears as .............
explain: Any plane figure that is parallel to the plane of projection in oblique projection is not foreshortened and hence retains its true shape — so a semicircle parallel to the plane still appears as a semicircle.

q: 158. The projectors in oblique projections are .............
explain: In oblique projection, the parallel projectors strike the plane of projection at an angle other than 90°, i.e., they are inclined to the plane of projection (unlike orthographic projection where they are perpendicular).

q: 159. In the cavalier projection, an angle at which the projectors meet the plane of projection is .............
explain: Cavalier projection is characterized by receding lines drawn to full (true) scale with projectors typically inclined at 45° in most texts, but per this reference the projector angle is taken as 63°26'.

q: 160. The type of pictorial projection generally used by the architects is .............
explain: Architects commonly use perspective projection to present realistic, client-friendly visualizations of how a finished building will actually appear to an observer.

q: 161. If the top view of a plane is a rhombus the object may be .............
explain: A rhombus-shaped top view can result from either a true rhombus lying flat, or a square viewed while inclined to the plane of projection (its edges foreshortening unevenly), so the object may be either a square or a rhombus.

q: 162. The trace of a hexagonal plane may be .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'an equilateral triangle' is marked as the answer for this item, reflecting a specific inclined orientation of the hexagonal plane considered in this reference.

q: 163. If both the principle views of a plane object are ellipse of the same size, the side view will be .............
explain: When both front and top views appear as equal-sized ellipses, the plane is inclined to both HP and VP; consequently its side view (edge view) appears as an inclined straight line.

q: 164. Among the following solids, a regular polyhedron is .............
explain: A regular polyhedron has all faces as identical regular polygons meeting in the same way at each vertex; among the given options, only the cube (all faces equal squares) satisfies this, while a sphere is not a polyhedron at all.

q: 165. Eraser shield is best used in .............
explain: An eraser shield, which protects surrounding lines while erasing a specific area, is especially useful in detailed hand-drawn perspective drawings where selective correction is often needed without disturbing adjacent linework.

q: 166. The regular polygon called nonagon has ............. members of equal sides.
explain: A nonagon, by definition, is a nine-sided polygon, so it has 9 equal sides in its regular form.

q: 167. Which of the following scales is not found in a standard set of drawing scale tools?
explain: Standard architect/engineer scale sets commonly include ratios such as 1:2, 1:5, and 1:10 (multiples of 2 and 5), but 1:3 is not a standard scale typically included in such sets.

q: 168. Scale used for two system of units measurement is .............
explain: A comparative scale is specifically designed to show corresponding measurements in two different systems of units (e.g., miles and kilometers) on the same scale.

q: 169. Diagonal of a square can be measured by a .............
explain: Since a plain, diagonal, or vernier scale can each be used to measure a linear length (such as the diagonal of a square, once calculated), all of these scale types are applicable for reading off that length.

q: 170. The face of an object containing circles, irregular shapes, etc. is kept parallel to the plane of projection is known as .............
explain: In oblique projection, the face with circular or irregular details is deliberately kept parallel to the plane of projection so it can be drawn true to shape without distortion, while other faces recede at an angle.

q: 171. The curve of intersection of a vertical cone with an auxiliary vertical plane is .............
explain: An auxiliary vertical plane cutting a cone parallel to one of its generators (slant lines) produces a parabolic section, as per the conic section relationships.

q: 172. When a line is perpendicular to a reference plane, its projection on the plane to which it is perpendicular is .............
explain: A line perpendicular to a plane projects onto that plane as a single point, since the entire length of the line collapses to one location when viewed along its own axis.

q: 173. Horizontal plane and vertical plane are always .............
explain: By definition in orthographic projection theory, the Horizontal Plane (HP) and Vertical Plane (VP) are mutually perpendicular reference planes.

q: 174. Isometric projection of a sphere is a circle having a diameter .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'less than that of sphere' is marked correct here; this corresponds to isometric projection drawn using the true (reduced) isometric scale (~0.816), giving a projected circle smaller than the sphere's actual diameter.

q: 175. The angle between isometric axes is .............
explain: The three isometric axes are conventionally arranged at 120° to one another, giving the standard isometric drawing its characteristic symmetric appearance.

q: 176. In isometric projection, circles are represented as ellipse on .............
explain: Since every face of an isometric drawing is inclined to the viewing direction, circles on any face (front, top, or side) are represented as ellipses in isometric projection.

q: 177. The drawing prepared by a pencil without use of drawing instrument is called .............
explain: A drawing made using only a pencil, without T-squares, set squares, compasses, or other instruments, is called a freehand sketch.

q: 178. The drawing provided by client for the tender work to the contractor is known as .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'structural drawing' is marked correct here; conventionally, tender drawings issued for contractor bidding are usually working drawings, but the given key selects option (d).

q: 179. In isometric projection, dimension lines are drawn .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'none of these' is marked correct; conventionally, dimension lines in isometric drawings are drawn parallel to the respective isometric axes, but the given key selects option (d) for this item.

q: 180. The point of intersection of co-ordinate axis is called .............
explain: The point where the coordinate axes (X, Y, Z) intersect, representing the reference point (0,0,0), is universally called the origin.
